newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said there would be a meeting between the Commission and the Dutch Presidency of the European Union on Tuesday morning. He said the meeting would be followed by a news conference at 1530/1430 GMT that would be retransmitted to the Breydel building press room.

Van der Pas said that Commission President Jacques Santer had welcomed U.S. President Bill Clinton's decision to postpone the application of a provision of the Helms-Burton Act but had underlined that the EU position in this matter would remain the same.

Spokesman Peter Guilford added that the EU position towards Cuba had not changed since the Dublin European Council. He added that the U.S.'s recent decision on Helms-Burton was not ultimately enough and that the EU would go ahead with the World Trade Organisation panel without a change in the timetable.

In answer to a question, Guilford said the composition of the panel would be decided by agreement between the U.S. and the EU authorities but that if no decision was reached, there would be arbitration by WTO Director General Renato Ruggiero.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/001: Response from Commission President Jacques Santer to the statement by U.S. President Bill Clinton on Helms- Burton.
- European Economy - Supplement A - No 12 - December 1996: The Community economic outlook: 1996-1998.
